entries.title: Convert an accepted abstract into a standalone session
entries.summary: Accepted abstracts can be turned straight into sessions again, without becoming subsessions. In **Program → Abstracts**, select abstracts and choose **More → Abstracts → Convert to session** (or **Actions → Convert to session** on an open abstract), then pick **This abstract becomes a session** to reclassify the same record (fields, participants, files, history and its evaluation all stay on it) or **Keep the abstract and create a linked session** to make a new session copied from it while the abstract keeps its evaluation.

where.path: Program → Abstracts → More → Convert to session

entries.use_case: Teams that ran their whole call for papers and review on abstracts can turn the accepted talks into sessions one to one, keeping the reviews, files and author order already on them, instead of nesting each one as a subsession under a parent.

cs_action.note: DIA and the American Society of Dentist Anesthesiologists noticed the old direct conversion was gone, and AHA asked for it; let them know it is back with a choice of mode.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to turn accepted abstracts into sessions without creating subsessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who collect abstracts and promote some of them to full sessions: DIA, ASDA, AHA.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Abstracts → select → More → Convert to session
internal.gotchas: Linked abstracts (Linked badge) can't be converted again. The linked-copy mode keeps the abstract's status, so an accepted abstract gives an accepted session. A role limited by session filters can only convert abstracts in its scope.
internal.talk_track: Select the accepted abstracts, choose Convert to session, and decide whether the abstract itself becomes the session or a linked session is created next to it. Either way nothing is nested and the reviews stay attached.

entries.title: Filter submissions on an evaluation plan's Review tab
entries.summary: The admin **Review** tab of an evaluation plan now has the same **Filters** evaluators see — for example track, tags or language — with a count per value, search for long lists, chips for what is applied, **Showing X of Y submissions** and **Clear filters**. Filters stay applied when you open a submission and come back, and the detail pane always shows a submission that matches.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Review

entries.use_case: Organizers reading feedback on a large plan (around 1,500 submissions) can narrow the Review tab to one track, tag or language and work through it inside Sessionboard instead of exporting to a spreadsheet.

cs_action.note: AHA asked for this for the AONL 2027 plan.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with a large evaluation plan exports to spreadsheets to read reviewer feedback by track or tag.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running high-volume Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans, starting with AHA (AONL 2027).
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Review → Filters
internal.gotchas: Filters come from the round's reviewer view settings, or from the plan's other rounds when this round has none; with none anywhere the button does not show. Exports do not follow the filters yet.
internal.talk_track: Open the Review tab and use Filters to see only one track or tag; the count tells you how many match, and the filters stay put while you click through submissions.

entries.title: Apply recommendations can set any status, including custom ones
entries.summary: **Apply recommendations** now has a **Set status to** section: choose the status that **Accept**, **Decline** and **Alternate** each set — any status in the event, including custom ones such as *Preliminarily Accepted* — or **Don't change status**. It starts from the round's recommendation settings and applies to that run only, and a warning shows when the choices would change nothing. Rounds with no saved mapping can now set statuses too.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Submissions → Apply recommendations

entries.use_case: Events that track decisions with custom statuses can move recommended submissions straight to the right one (for example Preliminarily Accepted) when applying reviewer recommendations, instead of applying the default and fixing statuses by hand.

cs_action.note: Synopsys (event 6822) asked for this; their Round 2 rounds had no saved mapping, so applying changed no status before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer applies recommendations and then re-sets statuses manually, or says Apply recommendations did nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using reviewer recommendations with custom submission statuses, starting with Synopsys.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Submissions → select → Apply recommendations
internal.gotchas: The choice applies to that run only; the round's saved recommendation settings are unchanged. Changing a status clears the preview.
internal.talk_track: When you apply recommendations, pick the exact status each decision should set, custom ones included, preview it, and apply.

entries.title: Building sessions from abstracts keeps each author's role and order
entries.summary: When abstracts became a session through a session build, a merge or **Assign to parent session**, the parent session moved each abstract's presenting author ahead of the authors listed before them. Roles and author order now carry over exactly, on the parent and on each subsession.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Builds, and Program → Abstracts / Sessions

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific meetings that build sessions from abstracts keep the presenting author and co-author order the submitter gave, so the program and printed agenda list authors correctly.

cs_action.note: IAS-USA (CROI 2027, event 6558) has one test session built before the 10-10 fix where two co-authors were saved as Presenting Author; that data is not changed by this fix.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports co-authors showing as presenting authors, or authors out of order, after building sessions from abstracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who build sessions from abstracts with custom author roles, starting with IAS-USA.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → [parent session] → Participants
internal.gotchas: Sessions built before the fix keep their existing participants. Exports that read the legacy speaker list still order by role.
internal.talk_track: Build your sessions from abstracts as usual; the presenting author and co-authors now keep their roles and order on the session.

entries.title: Approvals and upload slots: held files stay private, safer releases, slot rules on every move
entries.summary: Fixes from the Approvals beta readiness run. A file **Approvals** holds back (pending, changes requested or under a release time) can no longer be downloaded from its file link without signing in; **Copy link** is turned off for those files. Turning off **Require approval**, **Remove extra hold**, a later release time and bulk **Approve**/**Deny** now confirm first with how many files will change. **Save workflow** refuses a step nobody on the event team can review, and admins are emailed if a file ever lands on one. **Uploaded by** follows where the file was uploaded, so team members uploading in the speaker portal count as speakers. **Move to slot** follows the slot's file types, file limit and deadline (**Move anyway** for a passed deadline); speakers can still send a new version of a file sent back for changes after its slot is archived; and the session **Files** tab gains **Accept uploads after the deadline** for upload slots. The Files list shows the Session ID organizers know (SESS-2) and adds **Approve**, **Deny** and **Make visible** to row menus; times show the event time zone with its label, and portal slot cards show dates, file kinds and sizes in the portal language.

where.path: Publish → Approvals; Program → Settings → Files; Session → Files; Program → Submissions → Files

entries.use_case: Events running Approvals (beta) for press embargoes or sign-off — Advertising Week first — can rely on held files staying private until release, and admins get a confirmation before any click releases files to integrations.

cs_action.note: Approvals is beta: turn it on per event (Early Access). Advertising Week events 6023 and 6879 do not have it on yet. Existing data is not cleaned: 48 US + 2 EU slot/session pairs are over their file limit and 28 US images sit in PDF-only slots. Event 7141 has 2 files stuck on a step with no reviewers from before the fix; use Override or Add approver on them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer gates session files with Approvals or release times (press embargoes), uses upload slots with file-type limits, or asks why a file link stopped working (held files need a signed link until released).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Approvals beta (Advertising Week first) and any event using upload slots.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Files → Approvals; Event → Marketing → Email Campaigns
internal.gotchas: The db migration 20261022120000-approval-no-reviewers-notification-type.js must run before the no-reviewers runtime notification fires. Prod rows predating the fixes (over-limit slots, mistyped files) are not backfilled. The admin can override slot deadlines with force:true but cannot override file-type or limit rules.
internal.talk_track: Files under review now stay private until they are approved and released, every action that would release files asks first, and slot rules apply to admin moves as well as uploads.

entries.title: Send Email: one email per person when you pick contacts across a session and its subsessions
entries.summary: In **Send Email** from Sessions, with **Select Individual Contacts** and **Selected sessions and their subsessions**, a picked contact who sits on a session and one of its subsessions got one email per session. They now get one email, with the parent session's details, matching the **Send to 1 recipient** count on the confirmation. Two contact records sharing an address are also sent once. Role-based sends are unchanged: a speaker on three selected sessions still gets three session-specific emails.

where.path: Sessions → select sessions → Send Email

entries.use_case: Organizers emailing hand-picked speakers across sessions and subsessions send each person exactly one email, as the confirmation says.

cs_action.note: Reported by CTA (CES, event 6815, campaign 61305578): one picked contact received two delivered emails. Already-sent duplicates cannot be recalled.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a contact received the same campaign twice.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who emails hand-picked contacts from the Sessions grid.
internal.gotchas: The db migration 20261022120000-approval-no-reviewers-notification-type.js must run before the no-reviewers runtime notification fires. Prod rows predating the fixes (over-limit slots, mistyped files) are not backfilled. The admin can override slot deadlines with force:true but cannot override file-type or limit rules.
internal.talk_track: If you pick a person, they get one email — even if they are on both a session and its subsession.

entries.title: Shared report links show file names instead of raw URLs, and booklet schedules built from older templates now display sessions
entries.summary: Two display fixes ship together. **Shared report links** (the public URL generated from a saved report) now show a human-readable file name in file-type columns — such as **Company Logo** — instead of a raw CDN URL or `[object Object]`. Separately, **Print Agenda** booklets created from older starter templates that stored `confirmed` or `published` as session statuses now correctly match and display sessions on the schedule; previously those booklets printed an empty schedule.

where.path: Reporting → Shared report link (public URL) · Marketing → Print → [booklet] → Schedule

entries.use_case: Organizers who share report links externally no longer need to explain why file columns show garbled URLs. Teams using booklets built before the default starter was corrected no longer see a blank schedule when they export or share a program book.

cs_action.note: 45 booklet templates across 17 US events (5 edited in the last 30 days) were affected by the empty-schedule bug. Those booklets will now show sessions automatically — no action needed, but a heads-up to impacted customers is worthwhile. EU: 0 affected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their shared report link shows a raw URL in a file column, or that their printed program book shows no sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using shared/public report links with file-type columns, or any customer whose booklet was created from an older starter template.
internal.staff_path: Event → Reporting → [report] → Share link · Event → Marketing → Print → [booklet]
internal.gotchas: The shared-report file-name fix requires the companion UI change in lennd/sessionboard-web-ui-v2#1088 to be fully visible to users. The booklet fix is server-side only and takes effect immediately. CSV and XLSX exports from shared reports are unchanged — they still contain raw URLs.
internal.talk_track: Shared report links now display readable file names in file columns, matching what you see on the scheduled-report page. Booklets built from older templates will now correctly show your sessions on the schedule without any manual edits.

draft.docs_gap: The Print Agendas guide should note that booklet agenda blocks filter sessions by status, and that legacy starters using 'confirmed' or 'published' status values are automatically remapped to 'accepted'. The Reporting guide should mention that shared public report links render file-type columns as file names, consistent with the scheduled-report view.

entries.title: Rich-text instruction blocks display as formatted text in the reviewer submission view
entries.summary:
Rich-text blocks added to a submission form as static instructional content were showing raw HTML markup (e.g. `

Important Updates…

`) in the reviewer submission detail and **Print PDF** views. These blocks now render as formatted text, matching what submitters see on the form.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Submissions → [submission]

entries.use_case: When a submission form includes rich-text blocks with instructions or context for reviewers, those blocks now appear as readable formatted text rather than raw HTML tags. This is especially useful for forms with multiple instructional sections that guide reviewers through the scoring process.

internal.when_to_bring_up:
A customer reports that reviewers are seeing raw HTML tags (e.g.

, ) in the submission detail view or Print PDF instead of formatted text.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans whose submission forms include rich-text/instructional blocks.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → open any submission with richtext blocks
internal.gotchas: The bug was introduced in PR #155 on 2026-10-06, so only events whose forms were built or reviewed after that date are affected. The fix applies to both the on-screen submission detail and the Print PDF view.
internal.talk_track: If your submission form has instructional text blocks, reviewers now see them as formatted paragraphs — not raw HTML — both on screen and when printing to PDF.

draft.docs_gap: The "Reviewing a submission" section should note that rich-text instructional blocks from the form builder appear as formatted text in the reviewer submission detail and Print PDF views.

entries.title: Shared report links show file names instead of raw URLs
entries.summary: When a report containing file fields is shared via a public link, the **PublicReportPage** now displays each file as its readable name (linked) rather than a raw file URL. Search and sort on the shared page also use the file name.

where.path: Reports → [report] → Share → [public link]

entries.use_case: Organizers who share report links with stakeholders or vendors no longer need to explain raw file URLs — recipients see a clean, clickable file name in the shared view, matching what admins see inside the platform.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that people receiving shared report links see garbled URLs instead of file names in file-type columns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using shared report links on reports that include file-type fields.
internal.staff_path: Reports → [report] → Share link → open the public URL
internal.gotchas: The fix requires the API half (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4648) to ship the file_names field in the share data response; until that API change is live, the page behaves as before.
internal.talk_track: File columns in shared report links now show the actual file name as a clickable link — the same clean experience your team sees inside Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that file fields in shared (public) report links render as clickable file names, and that search and sort on the shared page operate on those names.

entries.title: Rounds in closed or past-deadline evaluation plans are now read-only
entries.summary: Reviewers could previously save scores on rounds whose evaluation plan was closed or had passed its deadline, even though **My Reviews** labelled those rounds "Closed · View only". Rounds in a closed plan or past a plan deadline are now fully locked: the **Closed · View only** label is enforced, and any write attempt returns a validation error. Team leaders and admins can still view the per-reviewer score breakdown regardless of plan state.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → My Reviews

entries.use_case: Events that close a plan or let its deadline pass need to guarantee no further reviewer edits slip through. Rounds in closed or expired plans are now locked server-side, so the "Closed · View only" label in My Reviews is always accurate and scores cannot be changed after the window ends.

cs_action.note: Prod US had 77 reviewer saves in the last 14 days on 3 rounds in closed-plan state (events 6589, 6678). Those rounds are now locked. Confirm with the event owners that those late saves are acceptable to discard going forward.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that reviewers were able to submit or change scores after a plan was closed or its deadline passed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans with defined plan deadlines or manual close actions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → My Reviews
internal.gotchas: Three events on Prod US (6589, 6678) had reviewers saving scores on closed-plan rounds in the past 14 days — those writes will now be blocked. Team leaders and admins retain full read access to the per-reviewer breakdown even when a plan is closed.
internal.talk_track: Once you close a plan or its deadline passes, the Closed label in My Reviews is now enforced end-to-end — reviewers cannot sneak in late edits, and your final scores are locked in.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that closing a plan or passing its deadline locks all associated rounds server-side, preventing any further reviewer writes, and clarify that team leaders and admins can still view score breakdowns on closed rounds.
draft.why_use_it: Evaluation plans let you run structured, multi-round review cycles with defined deadlines. Locking rounds when a plan closes or its deadline passes protects the integrity of scores already collected, so results you promote or export reflect only the reviews that were submitted on time.

entries.title: Ask is available on the public API, and AI can draft your event setup
entries.summary: Two new capabilities for organizers using Ask. First, a new **`POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask`** public API endpoint lets external AI assistants (such as ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot connected via MCP) query your event data — sessions, knowledge, Help Center articles and topic aggregates — and receive a structured answer with citations. Second, a new **Draft my setup** action generates suggested FAQ answers and flags content gaps (missing hotel, Wi-Fi, parking, accessibility info, etc.) from your published Info pages; the draft FAQ is saved with **Draft** status and is never surfaced to attendees until an organizer approves it.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Ask on the public API; then Settings → API Tokens → create a token and tick the Ask (organizer Q&A) scope (read:ask). It is not included in the read-only or all-scopes presets, so a token without it gets 403 SCOPE_REQUIRED.

where.path: External AI assistant (MCP) → ask_event tool, or the public API: POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask; Draft my setup on the event's Assistants page

entries.use_case: Teams using ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot as an MCP client can now ask questions about their event — sessions, speakers, knowledge base — directly from their AI assistant without switching to Sessionboard. The setup-draft feature helps organizers quickly populate their attendee FAQ by generating suggested answers and identifying gaps in their Info pages before the event goes live.

cs_action.note: The public API Ask endpoint and setup-draft feature require AI credits to be enabled for the org. Confirm the org has ai_credits configured before enabling.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about connecting ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot to their event data via MCP, or when they want help pre-populating their attendee FAQ before an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with AI credits enabled who are already using or evaluating MCP-connected AI assistants, and customers who want to accelerate their event knowledge-base setup.
internal.staff_path: Settings → API Tokens (tick the read:ask scope explicitly). Public route for integrators: POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask on the public API (public-api.sessionboard.com). Internal web-api routes (not for customers): POST /public-api/v1/event/:eventId/ask, GET/POST /assistant/event/:eventId/setup-draft
internal.gotchas: The Ask endpoint is always read-only (actions:[] is forced); it uses the token's user as the principal, not a body-supplied identity. The setup-draft FAQ is saved as Draft status and is never ingested or shown to attendees until an organizer explicitly approves it. Re-running setup-draft replaces the existing draft only while it is still in Draft status. A request already in flight (less than 10 minutes old) is reused rather than queued again.
internal.talk_track: You can now point your ChatGPT or Claude MCP client at your Sessionboard event and ask it questions about sessions, speakers and your knowledge base — it answers with citations and respects your credit budget. And before your event opens, you can run Draft my setup to get an AI-generated FAQ and a checklist of content gaps based on your Info pages, then review and approve before attendees ever see it.

draft.docs_gap: The Connect AI assistants guide should document the new ask_event MCP tool, the POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask endpoint contract (request body, response shape, error codes), the organizer-specific rate limits and credit budget, and the setup-draft GET/POST endpoints including how to review and approve the generated FAQ draft.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard lets you query your event data — sessions, speakers, knowledge articles and topic trends — from any MCP-compatible tool without leaving your workflow. Ask answers questions with citations so you can verify the source, and the organizer endpoint enforces the same rate limits and credit budgets as the in-product experience. The setup-draft tool analyses your published Info pages and generates a ready-to-review FAQ draft, flagging common gaps like missing venue, parking or accessibility details so nothing important is left out before attendees start asking.

entries.title: Five fixes: date formula filters, bulk language fields, interest-form filter picker, Tiers error messages, and Sign button contrast in dark mode
entries.summary: Five pre-release fixes shipped together: (1) **Preferences → Filter** on contacts and sessions now shows a date picker and date operators (is before, is after, etc.) when the filtered field is a date-formula field, instead of a number box. (2) **Title** and **Description** fields now appear in the bulk **Update language values** action for sessions, so translators can fill those fields in bulk like any other. (3) The field picker on the **Assignments** step of an Interest Form evaluation plan no longer overflows into the Impact Preview panel; the remove **×** button stays inside each filter rule. (4) When a **Sponsor Tiers** create, update, or delete fails, the toast now shows the server's reason instead of only a generic message. (5) The **Sign** button on the contract signing page is now readable in dark mode; its fill is automatically adjusted to meet 3:1 contrast against dark backgrounds while keeping the organizer's brand colour in light mode.

where.path: Sessions → Preferences → Filter; Contacts → Preferences → Filter; Groups → Sponsors → Tiers; Interest Forms → Evaluation Plan → Assignments; Contract signing page

entries.use_case: Teams using formula fields to compute dates can now filter sessions and contacts by those dates correctly. Multilingual programs can bulk-fill Title and Description translations. Reviewers assigning interest-form filters no longer fight a broken layout. Admins managing sponsor tiers get actionable error messages when a save fails. Speakers signing contracts in dark mode can see the Sign button clearly.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that filtering on a date formula field shows number operators, that Title/Description are missing from bulk language updates, that the interest-form filter layout is broken, that Tiers errors are unhelpful, or that the Sign button is invisible in dark mode.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using formula date fields in filters, language variants on sessions, interest-form evaluation plans, sponsor tiers, or the contract signing page in dark mode.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Preferences → Filter (date formula); Sessions → select rows → Update language values; Groups → Sponsors → Tiers; Interest Forms → Evaluation Plan → Assignments; Contract signing page (dark mode)
internal.gotchas: Date formula detection relies on output_type: 'date' or a legacy add_days root expression; numeric formulas like days_until keep number operators. The Sign button contrast fix only applies when the page renders in dark mode; light mode keeps the organizer's brand colour unchanged.
internal.talk_track: These are five targeted bug fixes from our pre-release audit. Date formula filters now behave like date fields, bulk language updates include Title and Description, the interest-form assignment layout is clean, Tiers errors are descriptive, and the signing page works in dark mode.

draft.docs_gap: The filter guide should note that formula fields with a date output type use date operators and a date picker, not number operators.

entries.title: Date formulas count days in the event's timezone and stay current every day
entries.summary: A formula built on **Date + N days** (`add_days`) now returns a date instead of a day count, and today is the calendar day in the event's timezone rather than UTC. Results that depend on today, such as **Days until**, recalculate every day shortly after local midnight without anyone saving the record, and clearing the source date clears the result.

where.path: Library → Fields → [field] → Field Type: Formula

entries.use_case: Teams that track visa expiries, deadlines or follow-up dates in formula fields get the right number for their own time zone, and it stays right on the days nobody edits the record.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer outside the Americas reports a Days until value that is off by one, a formula that never changes from the day it was saved, or a Date + N days field that shows a number.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Field Rules turned on that use days_until or add_days formulas.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Library → Fields → [formula field]
internal.gotchas: SB-9638 is still in QA: the grid filter on a Date + N days formula may still offer number operators until the follow-up web-ui-v2 PR ships. Recalculation only runs for events with Field Rules on that ended less than 30 days ago. add_days can no longer be used inside arithmetic; saving such a formula returns an error.
internal.talk_track: Date formulas now follow your event's time zone and refresh every night, so Days until is correct the morning after without anyone touching the record.

entries.title: Email Send Date tags use the event's calendar day
entries.summary: **Email Send Date** and the **+7 / +14 / +30 Days** tags now fill in the day the email goes out in the event's timezone (the organization's for organization-level campaigns), and add whole calendar days. A send late in the day UTC no longer prints the wrong date for an event in Asia or the Pacific.

where.path: Communications → Email campaigns → Merge tags

entries.use_case: Reply-by dates in campaign and automation emails match the calendar your recipients are looking at.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a "reply by" date in an email is a day early or late.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using the Email Send Date merge tags, especially events outside the Americas.
internal.staff_path: Event → Communications → Email campaigns → [campaign] → Merge tags
internal.gotchas: Only the fixed +7, +14 and +30 offsets exist; other offsets are not supported. UTC is used only when neither the event nor the organization has a timezone.

entries.title: Assign → Tasks stamps a due date relative to assignment
entries.summary: When you assign a task from a table with **Assign → Tasks** and leave the due date empty, each person now gets the task's **Due date relative to assignment**: the assignment day plus N days, at the end of the day in the event's timezone. A date you set on the assign screen wins, and assigning again keeps a date already stamped. Tasks that reach people through a portal's filters keep using the fixed **Due Date**.

where.path: CRM → Contacts → select records → Assign → Tasks

entries.use_case: Teams that give each speaker a personal deadline (for example seven days after they are asked) get that deadline when they assign in bulk, not only one record at a time.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer assigns tasks in bulk and finds no due date on the people they assigned, or asks why a task reached through a portal filter has the portal's fixed date.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events that use tasks with a due date relative to assignment.
internal.staff_path: Event → CRM → Contacts → Assign → Tasks; Portals → [portal] → Edit Tasks → pencil → Due date relative to assignment
internal.gotchas: Josh's decision: the relative date applies to direct assignment only. Portal-filter assignment uses the fixed Due Date.

entries.title: Filter What's New by module
entries.summary: **Community → What's New** has a **Module** menu above the feed. Pick **Program**, **Marketing** or any other module to see only its updates; **All modules** shows everything again. The menu lists only modules that have updates.

where.path: Community → What's New → Module

entries.use_case: Admins who only run part of the product can read the updates that matter to them without scrolling past the rest.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says What's New is too long to follow, or asks what changed in one area of the product.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization with Community.
internal.staff_path: Community → What's New

entries.title: Record Messages tab: resolve a thread, and the dot counts every unread message
entries.summary: A record's **Messages** tab now has a bar that shows whether the conversation is **Open** or **Resolved**, with **Mark resolved** and **Reopen**. The dot on the tab counts every unread message, so three new speaker messages read 3, not 1. Opening a thread from another event also loads that event's session content.

where.path: [record] → Messages tab

entries.use_case: Teams that work speaker messages from the record can close a conversation where they read it, and trust the unread count.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports the Messages tab dot under-counting, or asks how to close a conversation from the record.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event that uses record messages.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Submissions → [session] → Messages tab

entries.title: People automations can enroll only people with an incomplete portal task or form
entries.summary: In a People automation, **Only enroll when** now has **Portal assignment**: pick the **Item** (**Task** or **Form**), its **Name** and a **Status** (**Incomplete** or **Complete**), and only people whose portal task or form has that status are enrolled. **Clear** removes it.

where.path: Automations → [People automation] → When → Only enroll when → Portal assignment

entries.use_case: Reminder automations can go only to the speakers who still owe a task or form, instead of everyone whose field changed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants an automation to chase only people who have not finished a portal task or form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using People automations with portal tasks or forms.
internal.staff_path: Event → Automations → [People automation] → When

entries.title: Cancelling a scheduled campaign shows Cancelled straight away
entries.summary: After you cancel, pause or resume a campaign, or create a new schedule, the campaign page now shows the new status and the next send at once, instead of the old status until a reload.

where.path: Communications → Email campaigns → [campaign]

entries.use_case: Teams can trust that a cancelled campaign is really cancelled when the page says so.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer cancelled a campaign and still saw an upcoming send.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using scheduled or recurring campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Communications → Email campaigns → [campaign]

entries.title: Upload-slot reminders skip declined, withdrawn and cancelled sessions
entries.summary: Upload-slot reminders, the reminder preview, slot coverage and its CSV now leave out sessions that are **Declined** or in the decline queue, sessions with a custom status like **Cancelled** or **Withdrawn** under any base status, and withdrawn sessions. A participant who declined every role they hold on a session is not reminded either. Pending sessions are still reminded.

where.path: Program → Settings → Files → Upload slots → Reminders

entries.use_case: Speakers who are no longer presenting stop getting "upload your slides" emails, and coverage counts only the sessions that still owe a file.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports declined or cancelled speakers getting upload reminders, or a coverage count that looks too high.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event using upload slots with reminders.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Settings → Files → Upload slots; Program → Submissions → Files → Slot coverage
internal.gotchas: Custom statuses are matched by name (contains cancel or withdr), under any base status, so a Cancelled Onsite status under Accepted is excluded too. Pending sessions are still reminded; filter the slot on Status is Accepted to remind accepted sessions only.
internal.talk_track: Declined, withdrawn and cancelled sessions no longer get upload reminders, so only the speakers who still owe a file hear from you.

entries.title: History records SSO, two-factor, sign-in method and webhook changes
entries.summary: The **Audit** log in **History** now records SSO providers (create, edit, delete, signing certificates, per-event SSO on or off), requiring two-factor for the organization, member two-factor resets with the admin's reason, portal sign-in methods, and webhook endpoints. The **Type** filter offers **SSO provider**, **Webhook** and **Security setting** again, and **Action** offers **Two-factor reset**. Secrets, certificates and header values are never recorded.

where.path: History → Audit → Type / Action filters

entries.use_case: Security and IT reviewers can see who changed sign-in and integration settings, and when, without asking Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's security team asks for an audit trail of SSO, two-factor or webhook changes, or a security questionnaire asks about access-change logging.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with SSO, enforced two-factor, or webhooks, and anyone answering a security review.
internal.staff_path: Org → History → Audit; Event → History → Audit
internal.gotchas: Webhook changes made in the embedded Svix portal are recorded only once the Svix operational webhook is configured per region (SVIX_OPERATIONAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET); until then only changes through the API routes appear. Portal webhook entries show System as the user because Svix does not say who acted. No rows exist from before this release.

entries.title: The signing page follows dark mode and meets WCAG contrast
entries.summary: The Sessionboard e-sign page now follows the signer's light or dark setting, keeps the **Sign** button readable on any brand colour, starts with a **Skip to main content** link, respects reduced motion, and can be completed by keyboard alone.

where.path: Contract signing link → /sign page

entries.use_case: Signers on phones in dark mode, and signers who use a keyboard or screen reader, can read and sign agreements without help.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or their accessibility team asks whether the signing page meets WCAG, or a signer reports the page is hard to read.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers sending contracts with Sessionboard e-sign.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Contracts → [contract] → signing link
internal.gotchas: A dark-mode button edge and template field-type follow-ups are in a later web-ui-v2 PR.

entries.title: Contracts permission and Add Contract dialog no longer assume Docusign
entries.summary: The permission **Can create contracts (send via DocuSign or upload)** is now **Can create contracts (send for e-signature or upload)**, because it also covers Sessionboard e-sign. The **Add Contract** dialog names Docusign only on its Docusign tab. Nobody's access changes.

where.path: Org Settings → Team → Permissions → [role] → Contracts; [record] → Contracts → Add Contract

entries.use_case: Teams that use Sessionboard e-sign rather than Docusign can see the permission and the dialog cover their workflow.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why the permission label changed, or whether they need Docusign to send contracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Contracts; the change is automatic.
internal.staff_path: Org Settings → Team → Permissions → [role] → Contracts
internal.gotchas: The migration renames the row only while it still holds the original text; a hand-edited label is left alone.

entries.title: Your Country list and the event's phone country reach the public form and speaker portal
entries.summary: The organization's Country list (**Library → Fields → Country → Edit**) now applies on the public call for papers form and in the speaker portal profile, so hidden countries are not offered and renamed ones show your name. A value saved before you hid or renamed a country stays readable. The phone field on the public form starts on the event's country, from its timezone, instead of always on +1.

where.path: Library → Fields → Country → Edit; public CFP form; speaker portal → Profile

entries.use_case: Organizations that trim or rename the country list get the same list everywhere a speaker picks a country, and international speakers start on their own dialling code.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer hid or renamed countries and speakers still see the full list, or speakers outside the US complain the phone field starts on +1.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with a customised Country list, and events outside the US.
internal.staff_path: Org Settings → Library → Fields → Country → Edit
internal.gotchas: The phone default comes from the event timezone; there is no separate setting (Josh, SB-9636). Asia/Riyadh was added to the event timezone list.

entries.title: Call for Reviewers: approval calls keep invitees pending, and conflicts check Company Name
entries.summary: On a call with **Require approval** on, an invitee who accepts now waits as **Pending approval** and is enrolled, with their expertise picks on their tags, only when you **Approve**. Editing a profile without changing picks no longer clears them. Organization conflicts now compare the reviewer's affiliation with each session participant's **Company Name** (or Educational Affiliation), on the call and when you assign rounds.

where.path: Program → Evaluations → Call for Reviewers

entries.use_case: Committees that vet reviewers before they start keep control of who is enrolled, and conflict flags catch reviewers from a speaker's own institution.

cs_action.note: Rounds with the organization conflict rule on may show new organization flags (about 76 assignments in 6 US rounds on the replica dry-run). Let those customers know before they notice.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports invitees enrolled without approval, lost expertise picks, or no organization conflict where a reviewer and speaker share a company.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events running a Call for Reviewers, and any round with the organization conflict rule on.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluations → Call for Reviewers → [call]
internal.gotchas: New organization flags can appear on existing rounds; rounds set to exclude will exclude those pairs at the next assignment.

entries.title: Evaluation fixes: tagging every evaluator, and Interest Form filters
entries.summary: **Edit tags** on the Evaluators view now tags evaluators who joined through a portal or a round, and reports anyone skipped (**Tags updated for N evaluators. M skipped**). Interest Form **By submission** filters list Status values and the count follows the filters on every round.

where.path: Program → Evaluations → [plan]

entries.use_case: Large review committees can be tagged in one action, and plan settings behave the way the screen says.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's select-all tag edit failed, or an Interest Form filter showed no Status values.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Evaluation Plans v2.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluations → [plan] → Evaluators
internal.gotchas: Editing evaluator tags and affiliations now needs the evaluation plans update permission.

entries.title: Require disclosure is saved when you create an evaluation plan
entries.summary: Turning on **Require a disclosure from reviewers** in a new plan's Overview step is now saved with the plan. Before, the first save dropped it and the switch read off after a reload.

where.path: Program → Evaluations → New plan → Overview → Disclosures

entries.use_case: Accredited programs can require reviewer disclosures from the moment a plan is created.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer turned on Require disclosure on a new plan and it was off afterwards.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Disclosures on who run evaluation plans.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluations → [plan] → Overview

entries.title: A session save warns when a field rule could not apply
entries.summary: When you save a session and a field rule could not apply, a red **Saved, but a field rule was not applied** message now shows on the session page and in the side panel, instead of nothing.

where.path: Program → Submissions → [session] → Save

entries.use_case: Admins know when a rule they rely on did not run, instead of finding the wrong value later.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a field rule silently did nothing on a session.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Field Rules on.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Submissions → [session]

entries.title: Adding a participant who needs a mitigation opens the decision dialog
entries.summary: On a credit-designated session, adding one participant with relationships and no decision now opens the **Record mitigation** dialog right away. Save the decision and notes and the participant is added, with the decision on the **Mitigations** tab. Bulk adds from the directory still refuse with **Mitigation needed first**.

where.path: [session] → Participants → Add

entries.use_case: Accredited programs record the mitigation and add the faculty member in one step instead of leaving the session and coming back.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer running CE/CME asks why they cannot add a faculty member to a session.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Disclosures on and credit-designated sessions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Submissions → [session] → Participants

entries.title: Filter the Clips library by speaker, topic, aspect ratio and date
entries.summary: **Media → Clips** has a filter bar: **Speaker**, **Topic**, **Aspect** (16:9, 9:16, 1:1) and **Created from** / **Created to**. Speaker and Topic offer only values your clips have. When nothing matches, the page says **No clips match these filters** with **Clear filters**.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips

entries.use_case: Teams with large clip libraries can pull a speaker's vertical clips from one week in seconds for a post or campaign.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with many clips asks how to find the right one for a channel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with Clips.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips
internal.gotchas: Aspect matches only clips with a stored frame size. Clips exported before this release need Josh's backfill script (sb-9757-backfill-clip-media.js) before they appear under an aspect. Topics come from the session taxonomy once clips carry their session.

entries.title: Clip exports: animated captions render, posters on every clip, captions sized for 9:16 and 1:1
entries.summary: Clips with **Animated** caption styles, overlays and brand-kit exports now finish instead of failing. Every exported video clip gets a poster frame in the clips library and keeps the recording's session. On 9:16 and 1:1 clips and audiograms, captions are sized to the frame and stay in the bottom band, and long lines split into two-line captions. Recordings whose transcript came from a plain SRT or VTT open again, with untagged lines shown as **Speaker 0**.

where.path: Marketing → Media → [recording] → Edit & clip → Export

entries.use_case: Teams can export the social-ready, branded clips they designed without falling back to plain captions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an animated-caption clip stuck on Export failed, captions covering an audiogram waveform, clips without thumbnails, or a recording page that will not open after importing captions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations exporting clips and audiograms.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → [recording] → Edit & clip
internal.gotchas: Clips that failed before this release must be exported again. Existing clips get posters and session links only after Josh's backfill. A failed render now shows a readable message instead of a stack trace.

entries.title: Recaps generate for sessions that have a transcript but no summary yet
entries.summary: Generating a recap, podcast or Advocacy content for a session with a transcript and no AI summary now writes the summary first and then the recap, instead of failing with "capture it first".

where.path: Marketing → Live Transcribe → Recaps → Generate

entries.use_case: Teams that import transcripts can go straight to recaps without a separate summarise step.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sees "No AI summary exists for this session yet" on a session that has a transcript.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events generating recaps from transcripts.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Live Transcribe → Recaps

entries.title: Advocacy: shared card designs save to every card, LinkedIn shares count, bad links show a friendly page
entries.summary: Changing the colour, background, logo or font in a campaign's designer now saves and re-renders every card of that format, not only the tab you were on. LinkedIn and video shares now count as shares in attribution. A mistyped or malformed share link shows **This link isn't available** instead of an error. Attendee links accept `attend` as the platform for Sessionboard Attend registrations, with no email needed.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign]

entries.use_case: Speakers and attendees share the card you designed, and the share counts behind your sponsor and ROI reports are complete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sees two different card colours after editing a design, LinkedIn shares missing from attribution, or an error page from a share link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event running Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Edit campaign → Templates
internal.gotchas: LinkedIn shares from before this release need Josh's backfill SQL to appear as signals (12 US, 1 EU).

entries.title: The advocacy-attending embed accepts Sessionboard Attend registrations
entries.summary: The `advocacy-attending` widget now takes `source="attend"` with the registration's id, so an attendee who registered in Sessionboard Attend sees their share card on your confirmation page without an email in the link.

where.path: Embed code on your registration confirmation page

entries.use_case: Events that take registrations in Attend can show each attendee their share card right after they register.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using Attend registration asks how to put the attendee share card on their confirmation page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Attend registration and an attendee Advocacy campaign.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → [attendee campaign]
internal.gotchas: Waiting on the next embeds production release.

entries.title: Title slides: +N more at the ten-person maximum, and a deleted template no longer offers Regenerate
entries.summary: With **Show "+N more"** and a maximum of 10, a slide with 11 people now shows 10 and **+1 more**. On a session's **Files** tab, a title slide whose template was deleted says so instead of offering **Regenerate**, matching Presentations & files.

where.path: Marketing → Slides → [template] → Participants; [session] → Files

entries.use_case: Production teams see the full speaker list they asked for, and are not sent to regenerate from a template that no longer exists.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a ten-speaker panel showing fewer people, or a Regenerate button that does nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Slides.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Slides

entries.title: Program settings sheets stay open with your values when a save fails
entries.summary: When saving a tier, track, level, format, language, room or organization session catalog item fails, the sheet now stays open with what you typed and shows the reason, instead of closing as if it had saved.

where.path: Program → Settings → Tracks / Levels / Formats / Languages / Rooms

entries.use_case: Admins do not lose their typing or think a change saved when it did not.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a track or room they added disappeared.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Settings

entries.title: Keyboard reordering finishes long lists, Ask restores cut-off answers, sidebar labels fit, Publish shows both embed actions
entries.summary: Reordering with the keyboard in **Show/Hide Fields** and upload slots now moves a row all the way through a long list: **Space** or **Enter** picks it up, the arrows move it, **Home** and **End** jump, **Space** drops and **Escape** cancels. An **Ask** answer cut off by a dropped connection is restored when it reconnects. Long translated sidebar labels no longer clip, because the pin appears only on hover or focus. The event **Publish** page shows **New embed** and **Embed on your website** as separate actions.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Manage Fields → Show/Hide Fields; Program → Settings → Files; Ask; sidebar; Publish

entries.use_case: Keyboard and screen-reader users can reorder long lists, and teams using Ask during a busy event get the whole answer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports keyboard reordering stalling, an Ask reply cut off mid-sentence, truncated French sidebar labels, or a missing Publish action.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone; these are fixes with no feature gate.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → [portal] → Manage Fields → Show/Hide Fields; Event → Program → Settings → Files → Upload slots
internal.gotchas: Pointer drag is unchanged. Ask reconnect resync was not run against the live agents service before merge.

entries.title: Evaluations and reviewer portal labels use sentence case
entries.summary: Evaluation plan screens and the reviewer portal now use sentence case throughout, for example **Plan options**, **Show scores from other evaluators**, **Overall progress**, **Review rounds**, **Reviewer notifications**, **Under review** and **Pending payment**. German, Spanish and French were already right.

where.path: Program → Evaluations; Sites portal → My Reviews / Profile

entries.use_case: Customers who match our product copy in their own reviewer instructions see one consistent style.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Only if a customer points out inconsistent capitalisation in evaluation screens.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Evaluations or the Sites portal.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluations → [plan]; Sites portal → My Reviews
internal.gotchas: The portal half waits for the next org-portal release; reviewer instructions that quote the old Title Case labels may need updating.

entries.title: Ask refuses to move a form question onto a page that cannot show it
entries.summary: When you ask **Ask** to change a call for papers form, it can no longer put a People field on a session page (or the reverse). The change is refused with a clear message and nothing on the form changes, so a question can no longer vanish from the builder.

where.path: Ask → form changes

entries.use_case: Organizers who edit forms through Ask do not lose questions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a question disappeared from their form after asking Ask to add a condition.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events editing CFP forms through Ask.
internal.staff_path: Event → Ask

entries.title: Import an attendee list for Advocacy
entries.summary: On an event's **Attendees** page, **Import attendees** brings in a CSV or Excel list with the same importer contacts use. **Email** is required; **Registrant ID**, **Registration Status**, **Marketing Opt-in** and **Headshot** are optional, and re-importing updates attendees instead of duplicating them. Imported attendees can share Advocacy cards, with the imported headshot on their card.

where.path: Attendees → Import attendees (or Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign → Attendees → Import an attendee list)

entries.use_case: An event whose registration platform isn't connected to Sessionboard can still run an attendee Advocacy campaign: export the registration list, import it, and every opted-in attendee gets their own share card.

cs_action.note: Built for AVIXA, which has no attendee connector; tell them and any customer asking for attendee Advocacy without a supported registration platform.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants attendees sharing "I'm attending" cards but their registration platform has no Sessionboard connector.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy customers without a synced registration platform, starting with AVIXA.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attendees → Import attendees; the Attendees page needs Pathways Early Access, otherwise use the audience step's Import an attendee list.
internal.gotchas: Tick "These attendees agreed to receive marketing" (or map a Marketing Opt-in column) or nobody in the file can share. A withdrawn attendee is never opted back in by a file. Headshot URLs are linked, not copied.
internal.talk_track: Export your registration list, import it under Attendees with the opt-in ticked, then pick Attendees when you launch the campaign.

entries.title: Open link: attendees make their own Advocacy card
entries.summary: Turn on **Open link** on an Attendees campaign to get one link anyone can open to make their own card — they enter their name, email, company and job title and get it straight away, no attendee list needed. The signup page and the confirmation-page embed are in English, French, German and Spanish. Someone already on your list is emailed their own link instead, and a listed attendee who can't share gets no card.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → open an Attendees campaign → Share → turn on Open link

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Share → Open link

entries.use_case: Get attendees sharing that they're going without collecting or uploading an attendee list first — drop one link into a newsletter, the event website or the registration confirmation page.

cs_action.note: This is the Gleanin-style flow AVIXA asked for; walk them through turning it on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer uses (or is comparing us with) Gleanin, or has no attendee list in Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy customers running attendee campaigns, especially those without a registration integration.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share tab → Open link; Quick Launch and the campaign wizard also offer the switch.
internal.gotchas: The campaign has to be active for the link to work. With the open link on, a campaign can launch with zero attendees. Signups become attendees with source "advocacy". Confirmation pages that block scripts should link to the open link rather than embed the form.
internal.talk_track: Turn on the open link, copy it from the Share tab and put it anywhere attendees will see it — each person who opens it gets their own tracked card.

entries.title: Share tab for attendee campaigns, and email attendees their links
entries.summary: Attendee campaigns get a **Share** tab with everything you hand to attendees: the open link, the personal-link template for your registration platform (including an imported list), the personal-card and signup-form embeds, **Export CSV** of every attendee's personal link, and **Email attendees** — Notify now sends attendees their personal links. The Attendees audience is always selectable, with import and open-link options when nobody is eligible yet.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Share

entries.use_case: Everything needed to reach attendees — links for the registration email, embeds for the confirmation page, a mail-merge export, or an email from Sessionboard — is in one place on the campaign instead of in a setup guide.

cs_action.note: On for every Attendees campaign.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how attendees get to their share card, or wants Sessionboard to email attendees.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer running attendee Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share
internal.gotchas: The links export holds live sign-in links — treat it like a password list. Email attendees skips anyone not eligible (cancelled, waitlisted, opted out) and says why.
internal.talk_track: Open the Share tab, pick your registration platform and paste the personal link into your confirmation email — or click Email attendees and Sessionboard sends them.

entries.title: My Participation: one portal card with the real status of every submission
entries.summary: Every portal now shows a person's sessions, abstracts and applications in one **My Participation** card and tab, grouped by type and status (Pending, Declined, Accepted, Withdrawn) with **All / Abstracts / Sessions / Applications** chips. Each row shows the status your team set, custom statuses included. With participant acceptance on, anything still owed sits under **Pending Participant Confirmation**, and answered invitations read **Participant Confirmation Completed** and open the person's answers read-only.

where.path: Portal → Home → My Participation, and the My Participation tab

entries.use_case: Speakers see exactly where each of their submissions stands — in your own status wording — and which ones still need them to confirm, instead of a generic "Confirmed" or "Confirmation Needed".

cs_action.note: Every portal changes on deploy: the card and tab are renamed My Participation and declined submissions are a visible group. Portal Status Verbiage (Record Settings) and the portal Participation sections settings are retired; 4 events used the verbiage and 6 portals (one customer) had custom section titles.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why speakers see "Confirmed" instead of the real status, or wants speakers to see who still owes a confirmation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with speaker portals; most relevant with participant acceptance on.
internal.staff_path: Event → View Portal → View portal as a speaker
internal.gotchas: Custom Portal Status Verbiage and custom section titles no longer apply — the status label and fixed group names are used. Confirm only appears on accepted submissions.
internal.talk_track: Open the portal as a speaker: everything they are on is in My Participation, grouped by status, and anything they still owe you sits at the top with a Confirm button.

entries.title: Ask participants on accepted abstracts to confirm
entries.summary: A new **Enable Participant Acceptance for Abstracts** switch under Record Settings → Participant Acceptance asks the participants on an **accepted** abstract — including its submitting author — to confirm or decline in the portal, with the same invitations, accept-by deadlines and reminders sessions use. Off by default.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant portal → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance for Abstracts

where.path: Portal → My Participation → Pending Participant Confirmation → Abstracts

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific programs can get every presenting author to commit to presenting before they build the program, without emailing each one.

cs_action.note: Off by default; no abstract asks for confirmation until an admin turns it on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer accepts abstracts and wants authors to confirm attendance before the program is built.
internal.who_should_get_it: Abstract-based programs (medical, scientific) that use participant acceptance.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Participant portal → Participant Acceptance
internal.gotchas: Needs Enable Participant Acceptance on; turning that off clears this switch. Separate from the confirmation a presenting author gives when an abstract is placed into a session.
internal.talk_track: Turn on Enable Participant Acceptance for Abstracts and every accepted abstract asks its authors to confirm in their portal, with your deadlines and reminders.

entries.title: Order and group custom fields on contact, abstract and session profiles
entries.summary: Record Settings has a new **Profile layouts** tab. For the contact, abstract and session profile you can add named sections, move fields into them and drag fields into order; profiles in the event then show the **Custom Fields** card followed by one card per section. Without a layout, profiles stay A–Z in one card.

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Profile layouts

entries.use_case: Teams that track many custom fields — travel, disclosures, logistics — can find them in a sensible order and in labelled groups instead of one long alphabetical list.

cs_action.note: Nothing changes until an admin saves a layout.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer complains that custom fields on a contact or session are hard to find, or asks to group travel or logistics fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event with many custom fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Profile layouts
internal.gotchas: Applies to the session/abstract page, the session side panel and the event contact page. The org contact profile, the contact side panel and portals keep the A–Z order. Saving needs permission to edit event settings.
internal.talk_track: Open Profile layouts, add a Travel Information section, move the travel fields into it and save — every contact profile in the event now shows them together.

entries.title: Score Summary Report for Evaluation Plan 2.0, with co-review scores
entries.summary: Evaluation Plan 2.0 plans have a **Score Summary Report** in **Export**: one row per submission, lowest average first, with each reviewer's score, the average, the standard deviation, the comments, participants by role and the submission's dropdown fields, plus **Reviews complete** and **All reviews in**. When submissions are also reviewed in another plan, it adds **Scores in other plans**, their comments and combined average and deviation.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → plan → Export → Score Summary Report

entries.use_case: Program committees get a ranked, one-row-per-abstract score sheet — including co-review rounds in other categories — without building it from the individual grade export.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A committee chair wants a ranked list of scores and comments per abstract, or asks how to see co-review scores alongside the main plan.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Evaluation Plan 2.0, especially multi-category abstract reviews.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluation → plan → Export
internal.gotchas: Event plans only; organization (interest form) plans keep their two exports. Combined scores only combine plans that score on the same scale.
internal.talk_track: Export the Score Summary Report: every submission on one row with its scores, average, spread and comments, lowest first.

entries.title: Show only some assigned submissions in a portal
entries.summary: A portal's **Configuration** has a new **Visibility filter** under **Control Submission Visibility**. Add conditions — tags, status, track, format or a custom field — and the portal shows people only the assigned submissions that match, with a live count. Hidden submissions are hidden everywhere in that portal, including direct links.

enable.path: Portals → portal → Configuration → Control Submission Visibility → Visibility filter

where.path: Portals → portal → Configuration

entries.use_case: One portal can show speakers just the submissions that matter for it — say, only workshops — without splitting people into more portals.

cs_action.note: Off by default on every portal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants a portal to show only part of a speaker's submissions, e.g. only those with a certain tag.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running several portals or tracks per event.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → portal → Configuration
internal.gotchas: Your team still sees every submission in the admin. Turning Control Submission Visibility off still hides everything.
internal.talk_track: Turn on Visibility filter and add Tags contains Workshop — speakers now see only their workshop submissions in this portal.

entries.title: Assign a resource page to individual contacts
entries.summary: Resource pages can now be assigned to people, not only to portals: select contacts (or sponsors or exhibitors) → **Assign → Resources**. Once a page has individual assignments, only those people and portals that list it can open it. **Assigned contacts** on the resource card lists and removes assignments.

where.path: Contacts → select → Assign → Resources; Portals → Resources → ⋯ → Assigned contacts

entries.use_case: Send one person a page meant only for them — a visa letter or personal itinerary — without building a portal for them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer needs a page visible to a handful of speakers only.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using portal resources.
internal.staff_path: Event → CRM → Contacts → select → Assign → Resources
internal.gotchas: A page that is on a portal and individually assigned is listed once. Removing an individual assignment does not affect the portal assignment.
internal.talk_track: Select the speakers, choose Assign → Resources and pick the page — only they see it.

entries.title: Separate permissions for global and event-level fields
entries.summary: Field management is split per module into **Can manage event-level … fields** and **Can manage global … fields**. A role with only the event-level permission can add and edit its event's own fields, while global (organization-wide) and system fields are read-only for it. Every role that could manage fields keeps both.

enable.path: Event Team → Permissions → role → module → Can manage global … fields

where.path: Settings → Library → Fields; form builders

entries.use_case: Event teams can be trusted to add fields for their own event without being able to rename or delete the fields every other event shares.

cs_action.note: No access changed on deploy: every role with manage fields got the global permission too. Customers who want event teams locked out of shared fields must turn the global one off per role.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer had an event admin rename or delete a shared field, or asks to keep org fields locked.
internal.who_should_get_it: Multi-event organizations with shared global fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Event Team → Permissions → role
internal.gotchas: Event fields (the Events module) keep a single permission. The public API is unaffected — it authorizes by API token scope.
internal.talk_track: Turn off Can manage global session fields for the event team role — they can still add event fields, but shared fields are read-only for them.

entries.title: Export participants in their set order
entries.summary: The Sessions list has a new **All participants (in order)** column. It lists everyone on a session in the order you set — by drag or by participant ordering rules — each with their role, so exports keep that order instead of grouping by role.

where.path: Program → Sessions → Columns → All participants (in order)

entries.use_case: Abstract programs that keep authors in submission order can hand that exact author list to printers, apps and CME systems.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says exports show Presenting Author then Coauthors instead of the author order.
internal.who_should_get_it: Abstract-heavy medical and scientific programs.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → Columns
internal.gotchas: Read-only column; it never changes the stored order.
internal.talk_track: Add All participants (in order) to the Sessions list and export — the authors come out in the order you set.

entries.title: Require secure links on Awards URL questions
entries.summary: An Awards URL question's **Customize question** now has **Require secure links (https://)**. With it on, `http://` links are saved as `https://` from the form, admin edits, CSV import and the public API.

enable.path: Awards → program → Form Builder → URL question → … → Customize question → Require secure links (https://)

where.path: Awards → program → Form Builder → Customize question

entries.use_case: Links collected on nominations work and look trustworthy when reviewers or a winners page open them.

cs_action.note: Off by default per question.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer collects website or portfolio links on an Awards form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with URL questions.
internal.staff_path: Org → Awards → program → Form Builder
internal.gotchas: Existing links keep their address until edited.
internal.talk_track: Turn on Require secure links on the URL question and every link is saved as https.

entries.title: Session ID merge tag in new-submission and revision emails
entries.summary: The admin emails a submission form sends on a new submission and on a revision now offer a **Session ID** merge tag (`{{session_id}}`) — the ID the sessions grid shows, such as `SESS-123` — and include it in the default wording.

where.path: Submission form → Notifications → Admin notifications

entries.use_case: Your team can find a submission from the alert even after the submitter retitles it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer matches submission alerts to sessions by ID.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose team acts on submission alerts.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Forms → form → Notifications
internal.gotchas: Only the session submission form admin emails; interest form emails are unchanged. Edited templates need the tag added by hand.
internal.talk_track: Insert the Session ID tag in the New Submission email and your team sees SESS-123 in every alert.

entries.title: Automation trigger: participation acceptance status changed
entries.summary: People automations have a new trigger, **Participation acceptance status changed**, that fires when a participant accepts, declines or withdraws a session — in the portal, by your team, or by an overdue rule. Tick **Accepted**, **Declined** and/or **Withdrawn**, or none for any.

where.path: Automations → new People automation → When → Participation acceptance status changed

entries.use_case: Tell your team the moment a speaker declines, or send next steps to everyone who accepts, without checking the invitations list.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants to be alerted when speakers decline, or wants to email accepted speakers automatically.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using participant acceptance.
internal.staff_path: Event → Automations → New → People
internal.gotchas: Each answer is its own run, so declining two sessions enrolls the person twice. Enroll-existing backfill is not offered for this trigger.
internal.talk_track: Create a People automation on Participation acceptance status changed, tick Declined, and email your program chair.

entries.title: Sync selected sessions from the Sessions list, and grid and upload fixes
entries.summary: Selecting sessions on **Program → Sessions** now offers **Sync to …** (LiveBuzz, Visit and other session apps) under **More**, as the Agenda list does. Also fixed: the status picker in the grid respects a role's allowed status changes, the assigned-participant picker on file uploads only shows when participant assignment is on, and LiveBuzz sync history names the session and rule behind each removal.

where.path: Program → Sessions → select → More → Sync to …

entries.use_case: Admins can push just the sessions they changed to their event app from the list they work in.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to push a few sessions to LiveBuzz or Visit from the Sessions list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a session-syncing app.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → select rows → More
internal.talk_track: Select the sessions, open More and choose Sync to LiveBuzz — only those sessions update.

entries.title: Translate scorecards and round instructions for evaluators
entries.summary: On multilingual events, Evaluation Plan 2.0 round settings have a **Language variants** card for the reviewer instructions and each scorecard question's label, help text and option labels. Each review records the language it was written in, shown as a badge on the session's Reviews tab and as a **Review language** column in the Individual Grade Report.

where.path: Evaluation → plan → Rounds → round settings → Language variants

entries.use_case: International societies can let reviewers score in their own language while keeping one set of scores.

cs_action.note: Appears only on events with more than one enabled language.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An international customer has reviewers who do not work in the default language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Multilingual events using Evaluation Plan 2.0.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluation → plan → Rounds
internal.gotchas: No machine translation: blank translations fall back to the default language.
internal.talk_track: Open the round, pick Spanish in Language variants, translate the instructions and questions — Spanish-speaking reviewers see them.

entries.title: Evaluators choose their review language
entries.summary: On events with more than one language, the evaluator portal has a **Review language** menu on My Reviews, the round and the submission review. The screens, scorecard, instructions and submission fields switch to that language wherever a translation exists; untranslated values are marked **Shown in** the default language.

where.path: Evaluator portal → My Reviews → Review language

entries.use_case: Reviewers read and score submissions in their own language, which speeds reviews and cuts mistakes.

cs_action.note: Hidden on single-language events.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An international customer recruits reviewers who prefer another language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Multilingual events using Evaluation Plan 2.0.
internal.staff_path: Site → My Reviews (preview as an evaluator)
internal.gotchas: The choice is remembered per evaluator in their browser. Organization interest form rounds are not translated.
internal.talk_track: Your Spanish reviewers pick Español in the menu and see the scorecard and submissions in Spanish.

entries.title: Title, subtitle and voting banner colors on Sites
entries.summary: The Site builder's landing **Title** and **Subtitle** can each have their own color, and Branding has a **Community Voting banner text color**. These are used exactly as chosen, with a contrast warning under 4.5:1. **Text Color** now warns when it is hard to read and says which color the Site shows instead.

where.path: Site builder → Landing → Title / Subtitle → Set a color

entries.use_case: Brand teams can match the landing headline to their style guide, and know before publishing when a color will be hard to read.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says Text Color does nothing, or wants a different headline color.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a Site.
internal.staff_path: Site builder → Landing; Site → Branding
internal.gotchas: Text Color is still swapped for white or dark text when it reads under 4.5:1; the explicit title, subtitle and voting colors are not.
internal.talk_track: Set the Title color in the Site builder — the preview updates, and the builder warns if it is hard to read.

entries.title: "Participant" labels, existing-contact email and Site checks
entries.summary: Record Settings now says **Participant portal** and **Participant Headshot Limitations**, and Speaker Feedback is **Participant Feedback**.
